steps.text: Whisk together Worcestershire sauce, liquid smoke, salt, seasoned salt, garlic powder, and onion powder in a bowl until the salts have dissolved.
To use, pour the marinade over up to 2 pounds of meat in a resealable plastic bag. Seal the bag, and refrigerate overnight. The following morning, discard the marinade, and cook the meat as desired.

raw_recipe.headline: Smoky Steak Marinade
raw_recipe.description: This is a rich, smoky tasting marinade!
raw_recipe.name: Smoky Steak Marinade

recipeInstructions.text: Whisk together Worcestershire sauce, liquid smoke, salt, seasoned salt, garlic powder, and onion powder in a bowl until the salts have dissolved.
To use, pour the marinade over up to 2 pounds of meat in a resealable plastic bag. Seal the bag, and refrigerate overnight. The following morning, discard the marinade, and cook the meat as desired.

review.reviewBody: This can be a great marinade if you don't use all the salt or all the powders! I cut the recipe in half for a 1 lb. sirloin steak. I didn't use any table salt and only half of the seasoned salt (basically 1/4 of what the original recipe called for. I used minced garlic and added 2 Tbsp. of olive oil. I let this marinate all day. The result was a very flavorful, tender, smoky cut of steak and sirloin is not the best cut of meat either so I was pleasantly surprised. I would definitely try this again but on strips or rib eyes.
I left out the salt and used only a tablespoon of the seasoned salt. I cooked it with cubed steak in the slow cooker and it was absolutely delicious!

Used this marinade for 12 boneless chicken thighs and loved how tender and flavorful the meat was. I did however, take the advice of the other reviewers and cut the salt way down to 1 1/2 tablespoons of season salt and no table salt. Next time I'll substitute the garlic powder for fresh garlic. Thanks for sharing Chase.

WAY TOO SALTY. I was suspicious that it had too much salt, and the results verified it. It also had too much liquid smoke in it. It does not need the regular salt and the liquid smoke needs to be cut by 1/2. The steak was marinated for 12 hours, and probably would have been inedible if was for 24 hours.

Made this and did not use no where near as much salt. Used only one tsp. Added about a tbsp of pepper. All other measurements as to the recipe. Had to add one cup of water to this mixture as it turned into a thick paste. I will be trying the meal at lunch. Here's hoping.

Nice smoky flavor BUT way too salty. I kinda thought it may be so I had reduced the seasoned salt to 2T and increased the garlic powder (we really like garlic.) It was still just on the edge of being too salty to eat. Will definitely make again but decrease the seasoned salt to 1T, maybe add some of my own seasonings and some chopped garlic cloves. Cooked up really well though. Took a photo but my phone apparently doesn't take a large enough file, lol.

way too much salt. I'm going to try this marinade again but I'm going to omit the table salt and use half or less of the season salt. Hopefully that change will make it taste as good as it sounded when I first read it.
We let our frozen chicken breasts sit in this marinade all day and cut them up into strips before baking. Wonderful! Thanks! We will use this marinade often.

This was WAY TOO SALTY and I only used the seasoning salt, nota adding the regular. Going by what others said, I thought I'd cut way back on the salt, and our beef tenderloins that I marinated overnight were inedible....What a waste of money!! I'm sorry, but this was AWEFUL!!!

We halved the recipe and marinaded two 5-ounce filets for about 2 hours and they were incredibly delicious. It was pretty salty, which I love, but you might want to put 1/2-3/4 the amount of salt in it if you like yours less salty.

This is pretty good stuff. I did cut back the salt to 1 tsp of seasoned salt and whish I would have added just a bit more. It has a good smokey flavor and went through the meat very well. DH grilled these for us and we enjoyed them.
It is a EXCELLENT MARINADE ON STEAKS!!!😊🇨🇦 it makes the steaks taste so delicious and tenderizes anything.
Really tasty with MF tacos boiii

This was absolutely inedible. I should have known better when I saw how much salt was in it. This recipe ruined some very fine cuts of steak that I was serving to other people. Please don’t use this recipe.

Way too salty, I even cut all the salt that wasn't seasoned salt and still way way way too salty. 

It's not meant to be a brine but that's basically what it is without the water.
I marinated steaks with this and my family did not like them at all. They were too dry and tasted more like low quality beef jerky. Will not be using this recipe again.
Very, very salty! This recipe has potential but needs tweaked a bit.

For me the flavor is too strong to use as a marinade and I only marinated my steak for 45 minutes! Think it would work better as a sauce to baste your meat with while cooking. The flavor is good, 'am trying to think of a way to tone it down a bit.

I think this recipe calls for wayyyy too much salt. After reading the reviews, I decided to cut out the table salt all together and reduce the seasoned salt to just one tablespoon. Next time I will use fresh garlic instead of garlic powder. All the "powders" made the marinade pretty thick. I like the concept of this marinade, it just didn't work out that well for me.

I love a salty steak, but this is even too much. I didn't even use all the salt listed in the recipe and ours was still way too salty. I only marinated it for an hour, I can't even imagine how bad it would have been if I'd done it overnight.
